proposals.after: In the seventh month Chanzhou fell to him.

proposals.before: In the eighth month Liang recovered Cao. Jin and Liu Yan faced off at Xin; Jin taunted him day after day, but Yan barred his gates and would not fight.
proposals.after: In the eighth month Liang recovered Chanzhou. Jin and Liu Yan faced off at Xin; Jin taunted him day after day, but Yan barred his gates and would not fight.
proposals.reason: Chinese 澶州 is Chanzhou; the English Cao is the wrong prefecture.

proposals.before: In the eighth month Liang retook Cao Prefecture. The Jin and Yan armies faced each other at Xin; the Jin army repeatedly challenged battle, but Yan shut his walls and would not come out.
proposals.after: In the eighth month Liang retook Chanzhou. The Jin and Yan armies faced each other at Xin; the Jin army repeatedly challenged battle, but Yan shut his walls and would not come out.
proposals.reason: Chinese 澶州 is Chanzhou; the English Cao Prefecture is the wrong place.

proposals.before: In the eleventh year, the Prince of Yan Liu Shouguang was killed at Taiyuan, and his father Rengong was used at Yanmen.
proposals.after: In the eleventh year, the Prince of Yan Liu Shouguang was killed at Taiyuan, and his father Rengong was offered in sacrifice at Yanmen.
proposals.reason: 用…于鴈門 plus the note 剖心以祭墓 means sacrificial offering, not merely 'used'.

proposals.before: Khitan horsemen raided Weizhou and captured Li Siben, military governor of Zhenwu.
proposals.after: Khitan horsemen raided Yuzhou and captured Li Siben, military governor of Zhenwu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 蔚州 is Yuzhou, not Weizhou (魏州/衛州).

proposals.before: The Khitan raided Weizhou and seized Zhenwu military governor Li Siben.
proposals.after: The Khitan raided Yuzhou and seized Zhenwu military governor Li Siben.

proposals.before: In the first month of the eighteenth year a Wei prefectural monk, Zhenzhen, presented one Tang Mandate of Heaven treasure.

proposals.before: On xinhai of the intercalary month he enfeoffed his brothers: Cunmei as Prince of Yong, Cunba as Prince of Yong, Cunli as Prince of Xue, Cunwo as Prince of Shen, Cunyi as Prince of Mu, Cunque as Prince of Tong, and Cunji as Prince of Ya.
